line: Sharp nose, low grip. It turns now and slides if you stay flat.
character: A short, nervous car. The wheel answers immediately, and a bend will shove it if you do not lift.

line: The balanced car. Nothing here is a trap.
character: Every number sits near the middle. It is the car that forgives a late turn and a messy exit.

line: Long and calm. It holds a line and gives up a little pace.
character: The Vantage trades launch for grip. Turn in a moment early. Once it is pointed, it stays there.

line: Planted. The wheel is slow, so commit before the bend.
character: Grip is the point of this car. It will not flick into a coin at the last moment.

line: A straight-line car. The tyres let go before the pace does.
character: Use the Huracán where the road is open. In a bend, lift or it walks toward the grass.

line: Light, sharp, and happy to stop.
character: The 750S rotates and then the brakes finish the job. It is the car for a late dodge around a hurdle.

line: Huge pace, heavy nose. Plan the bend before you arrive.
character: The Chiron wins the clock on a straight and loses time if you ask it to change its mind.

line: The fastest car here, and the loosest.
character: It launches hard, it points instantly, and the tyres give up. Hit the coin, then get straight before the next bend.

line: Brakes and grip first. It stays where you point it.
character: The Huayra gives up the last bit of pace so a hurdle is a choice, not a surprise.
The R8 does not lead any column. That is why it is easy to put on a coin and still meet the clock.

line: Launch and grip. The nose turns after the power arrives.
character: The GT-R jumps off the line and sticks in the bend. Leave extra room to steer out for a coin.

line: Light and pointy. It changes direction and does not glue down.
character: The MC20 is for weaving. Grip is ordinary, so do not combine a coin dive with a flat-out bend.

line: The slowest and the widest. It holds a line, then runs out of clock.
character: The Continental is stable and late. Skip a coin if it sits inside a bend. The clock is the real opponent.

line: Strong pace, weak brakes, low grip. Lift early.
character: The Corvette arrives at a hurdle still carrying speed. Brake before you see the stripes, not when you reach them.

line: A heavy coupe that stops and sticks. Steering is what you wait on.
character: The M8 trusts its brakes and its tyres. Start the turn sooner than feels natural.

line: The strongest launch, and a heavy body after it.
character: The Taycan is at pace before the others have cleared the launch pad. A hurdle then costs more, because there is more mass to wake back up.
